**Kelly Bishop** (born **Carole Jane Bishop** ;[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-1) on February 28, 1944) is an American [actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actress "Actress") and [dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance "Dance"), best known for her roles as [matriarch Emily Gilmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emily_Gilmore "Emily Gilmore") on the series _[Gilmore Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilmore_Girls "Gilmore Girls")_ and as Marjorie Houseman, the mother of [Jennifer Grey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Grey "Jennifer Grey")'s Frances "Baby" Houseman, in the film _[Dirty Dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_Dancing "Dirty Dancing")_. Bishop originated the role of Sheila in _[A Chorus Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Chorus_Line "A Chorus Line")_ for which she won a [Tony Award for Best Performance by a Featured Actress in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Performance_by_a_Featured_Actress_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Performance by a Featured Actress in a Musical"). In 2023, she starred as Mrs. Ivey in _[The Watchful Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Watchful_Eye "The Watchful Eye")_ (2023).
## Early life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kelly_Bishop&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]
Bishop was born on February 28, 1944, in [Colorado Springs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Springs,_Colorado "Colorado Springs, Colorado"), [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-2) She grew up in [Denver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver "Denver"), [Colorado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado "Colorado"), where she trained to be a [ballet dancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballerina "Ballerina"), and as a teenager, moved to California attending the [San Jose Ballet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jose_Ballet "San Jose Ballet") School. At 18, she headed to [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") and landed her first job dancing in a year-round [ballet company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballet_company "Ballet company") at [Radio City Music Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radio_City_Music_Hall "Radio City Music Hall"). Bishop continued to dance in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Valley "Las Vegas Valley"), [summer stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_stock_theatre "Summer stock theatre"), and on television until she was cast in 1967 in _[Golden Rainbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Rainbow_\(musical\) "Golden Rainbow \(musical\)"),_ her first [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") role.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-book-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-4)
## Career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kelly_Bishop&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Bishop moved to New York City to try to become a ballet dancer.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-book-3) Bishop's big break came when she was cast as the sexy, hard-edged Sheila in the 1975 Broadway production of _[A Chorus Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Chorus_Line "A Chorus Line")_ , for which she won the [1976 Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Featured_Actress_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Featured Actress in a Musical") as "Best Supporting or Featured Actress (Musical)" as well as the 1976 [Drama Desk Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_Desk_Award "Drama Desk Award") for "Outstanding Actress in a Musical". Many details of the character Sheila's past were drawn from Bishop's real life, as she helped develop the character during early workshops.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-book-3) She was also cast in Broadway productions of _[Six Degrees of Separation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Six_Degrees_of_Separation_\(play\) "Six Degrees of Separation \(play\)")_ , [Neil Simon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Simon "Neil Simon")'s _[Proposals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proposals_\(play\) "Proposals \(play\)")_ , the Tony Award-winning [_The Last Night of Ballyhoo_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_last_night_of_ballyhoo "The last night of ballyhoo"), and _[Bus Stop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_Stop_\(play\) "Bus Stop \(play\)")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-5)
In film, she was cast opposite [Jill Clayburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jill_Clayburgh "Jill Clayburgh") in [Paul Mazursky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mazursky "Paul Mazursky")'s big-screen drama _[An Unmarried Woman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An_Unmarried_Woman "An Unmarried Woman")_ (1978). In the 1987 film _[Dirty Dancing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dirty_Dancing "Dirty Dancing")_ , she was originally set for a small role, but took on the much bigger role of Mrs. Houseman when [Lynne Lipton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lynne_Lipton "Lynne Lipton") (originally cast to play the role) fell ill during the first week of shooting.
Bishop went on to play mothers to high-profile stars in features: [Howard Stern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Stern "Howard Stern")'s in the [Betty Thomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Betty_Thomas "Betty Thomas")-directed comedy _[Private Parts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_Parts_\(1997_film\) "Private Parts \(1997 film\)")_ (1997), and [Tobey Maguire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tobey_Maguire "Tobey Maguire")'s in _[Wonder Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_Boys_\(film\) "Wonder Boys \(film\)")_ (2000). Additional feature credits include _Ich und Er_ (USA: _Me and Him_ , 1988), _[Queens Logic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens_Logic "Queens Logic")_ (1991), _[Cafe Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cafe_Society_\(1995_film\) "Cafe Society \(1995 film\)")_ (1995), _[Miami Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Rhapsody "Miami Rhapsody")_ (1995) and _[Blue Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Moon_\(2000_film\) "Blue Moon \(2000 film\)")_ (2000).
Bishop debuted on television in _[Hawaii Five-O](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii_Five-O_\(1968_TV_series\) "Hawaii Five-O \(1968 TV series\)")_. She starred in the [Mike Nichols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Nichols "Mike Nichols") series _[The Thorns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Thorns_\(TV_series\) "The Thorns \(TV series\)")_ in 1988. She played [Lisa Ann Walter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Ann_Walter "Lisa Ann Walter")'s mother on _My Wildest Dreams_ in 1995. She guest-starred on, among other series, _[Kate& Allie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kate_&_Allie "Kate & Allie")_, _[Murphy Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murphy_Brown "Murphy Brown")_ , _[Law& Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_&_Order "Law & Order")_, and _[Law& Order: Special Victims Unit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Law_&_Order:_Special_Victims_Unit "Law & Order: Special Victims Unit")_.
From 2000 to 2007, Bishop starred in [The WB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_WB "The WB")/[CW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CW_Television_Network "CW Television Network") series _[Gilmore Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilmore_Girls "Gilmore Girls")_ as wealthy [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England") matriarch [Emily Gilmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Gilmore_Girls_characters#Emily_Gilmore "List of Gilmore Girls characters"). Both she and fellow series regular [Edward Herrmann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Herrmann "Edward Herrmann") were [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/30th_Tony_Awards "30th Tony Awards") recipients in 1976.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-6) She reprised her role in the 2016 miniseries _[Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilmore_Girls:_A_Year_in_the_Life "Gilmore Girls: A Year in the Life")_ on Netflix. She would later reunite with [Amy Sherman-Palladino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amy_Sherman-Palladino "Amy Sherman-Palladino"), who created _[Gilmore Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilmore_Girls "Gilmore Girls")_ , on _[Bunheads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunheads "Bunheads")_ ,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-7) which aired from 2012 to 2013 and was canceled after the first season. Bishop has since appeared in television shows including _[Army Wives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Army_Wives "Army Wives")_ , _[Mercy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercy_\(TV_series\) "Mercy \(TV series\)")_ , _[The Good Wife](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Good_Wife "The Good Wife")_ , and played Benedetta in the Golden Globe-winning series _[The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Marvelous_Mrs._Maisel "The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel")_ , where she was again reunited with Sherman-Palladino. Bishop starred in the TV drama series _[The Watchful Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Watchful_Eye "The Watchful Eye")_ (which premiered on January 30, 2023) as Mrs. Ivey.
Following the end of _Gilmore Girls_ , Bishop returned to theater, performing in _[Becky Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Becky_Shaw "Becky Shaw")_ at the [Second Stage Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_Stage_Theatre "Second Stage Theatre") in 2008 and as Evangeline Harcourt in the 2011 revival of _[Anything Goes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anything_Goes "Anything Goes")_ alongside [Sutton Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutton_Foster "Sutton Foster") and [Joel Grey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joel_Grey "Joel Grey"), as well as appearing in the 2011 movie _[Friends with Kids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends_with_Kids "Friends with Kids")_.
In 2024, Bishop wrote a debut novel called _Broad Appeal_ , with Ali Rosen and William Morrow.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-8)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kelly_Bishop&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]
Bishop resides in [South Orange, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Orange,_New_Jersey "South Orange, New Jersey"). She was first married to stagehand and electrician Peter Miller in 1970 before divorcing in 1975.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-book-3) She was married to the TV [talk show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talk_show "Talk show") host [Lee Leonard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Leonard "Lee Leonard") until his death in 2018.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_Bishop#cite_note-10)
Bishop grew up on a farm.
